claims.text: Elemental Cr coatings on zirconium-alloy cladding can peel and crack during high-temperature steam oxidation.
Premature failure of the baseline Cr coating is caused by elevated-temperature Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
The proposed intervention is to deposit a thin alumina interlayer on the zirconium-alloy substrate before depositing Cr.
Atomic layer deposition can provide the required controlled-thickness, conformal alumina interlayer.
The deposited alumina interlayer will be continuous and dense.
Alumina provides a chemically inert and thermally stable interface between Cr and zirconium alloy.
A dense interfacial barrier can limit atomic transport and suppress interdiffusion.
An alumina interlayer will suppress mutual Cr-Zr interdiffusion during high-temperature steam exposure.
Suppressing Cr-Zr interdiffusion will prevent formation of deleterious Cr-Zr intermetallic phases.
Preventing interdiffusion and intermetallic formation will mitigate coating adhesion loss and cracking during accident conditions.
The alumina interlayer will not interfere with the corrosion protection supplied by Cr under normal subcritical-water operation.
Relative to the unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the alumina-interlayered coating will exhibit measurably less Cr-Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the baseline, the alumina-interlayered coating will have markedly improved adhesion and structural integrity after high-temperature steam exposure.
The modified coating will maintain effective corrosion protection during long-term subcritical-water exposure.
Typical subcritical-water reactor operation is represented by a temperature around 300 degrees Celsius.
The intervention is intended to remain effective in accident-relevant steam approaching or exceeding 800 degrees Celsius.
